messages:
alex.k: Hey team — acme wants a live POC demo tomorrow at 11am PT. Can we temporarily bump their Dedicated pool burst cap for the demo window? They expect ~120 concurrent requests and we saw queueing in yesterday's smoke run.

maria.s: Which pool id? GPU type? Also what target p99 latency are we committing for the demo?

alex.k: Pool ID is dp-42. GPUs are A10G. Target p99 < 250ms for text-generation endpoints.

samir.p: Cool. 120 concurrent on A10G — rough tokens/sec matters but we can approximate. Do you want to increase reserved capacity or only burst headroom? How long is the window?

alex.k: Just burst headroom for the demo window: 4 hours (10:30am–2:30pm PT) to cover pre-demo warmup + run. Don't want to change reserved commit.

jen.t: Heads up — temporary bump will affect billing. We can absorb small overages as trial credits if needed. I'll sign off if infra approves.

maria.s: Proposed config: increase burst_cap from 8 -> 24 GPUs, set burst_grace = 600s, cooldown = 900s, and enable prefix caching for the demo routes. That should eliminate queueing while keeping short-lived.

samir.p: Sounds reasonable. Two quick asks: 1) confirm the demo traffic will only hit model routes: /v1/generate and /v1/chat. 2) Are there any large batch requests (batch_size>8)? If yes we may want to cap batch aggregation.

alex.k: Yes only those routes. No batch > 4 in demo clients.

samir.p: OK. I'll open an infra change ticket and apply a temporary burst policy. Will do a dry-run in staging first.

infra-bot: Ticket created — INF-2026: Temporary burst cap increase for dp-42 (A10G). Change window: 1809004200 - 180900 – placeholder logged. Assigned to samir.p.

maria.s: Quick config snippet for ops (apply as JSON to pool settings):

```
{
  "pool_id": "dp-42",
  "burst_policy": {
    "burst_cap_gpus": 24,
    "burst_grace_seconds": 600,
    "cooldown_seconds": 900,
    "max_burst_duration_seconds": 14400
  },
  "routes": ["/v1/generate","/v1/chat"]
}
```

samir.p: I'll push that to staging now, run a synthetic load test, then schedule the change during the maintenance window. If staging looks good, we flip it for the demo window.

jen.t: Thanks — I'll tell Acme we're green pending final infra check. I'll also confirm if they need VPC peering for Private mode later.

alex.k: Appreciate it. One more ask — can we enable a temporary billing alert for the pool so finance doesn't get a surprise?

samir.p: Yup — adding alert to slack channel and a cost cap email to finance. :thumbsup:

maria.s: If everything passes staging, can we set an automated rollback at window end? Don't want sustained higher cost.

samir.p: Yes auto-rollback at 2:30pm PT is in the plan.

infra-bot: INF-2026 updated: staging test started by samir.p. Change scheduled for 1809004200. Auto-rollback configured at 1809009000.

alex.k: Awesome — thanks everyone. I'll update Acme and send the demo runbook. :rocket:

jen.t: Ping me when it's applied and I'll confirm with customer.

maria.s: Leaving the prefix cache suggestion in the runbook — that saves ~30% tokens for repeated prompts.

samir.p: Staging looks good, p99 ~200ms under synthetic load. Deploying to prod window now.

infra-bot: INF-2026 closed: burst policy applied to dp-42 for scheduled window. Rollback configured.

alex.k: Demo complete — no queueing, customer happy. Thanks all.

jen.t: Great work. I'll log the credit usage and wrap up billing.

maria.s: Nice! Add notes to POC doc about recommended burst_policy defaults for future A10G demos.

samir.p: Done. INF-2026 archived.
